accepts.because: a turn that entered from outside this member -- an operator, a digest, a second person's agent -- on its way to the screen. It meets the firewall before it meets anything of this member's, which is the whole reason the firewall sits at this level: two channels of one person need ONE view of an attacker, and the rate window must not restart because a generation was replaced. The caller should promote `context.channel` (and `context.user_id` where this colony has per-user rules); the door edge promotes what it finds and falls back to the empty string, so an unpromoted channel costs one shared rate bucket rather than a vanished turn

a question against this member's memory from outside the member. The lane is named for the asker's side of it -- the level turns it into the hive's own `in_query` at the door -- and since GH #533 the answer LEAVES THIS LEVEL: the bundle on `bundle`, the refusal on `reject`, both addressed back to the outside asker by the reply-to token this door stamps, `context.recall_caller = 'outside'` (ADR-0019). The door STAMPS that token rather than carrying what the caller sent, because the value space of the token at this boundary is this level's own: an outside caller with several askers of its own tells its rounds apart on a hop key of its own, which crosses the hive untouched -- this door promotes no correlation at all, because since GH #552 the `in_query` lane has ONE meaning and the hive's own `bundle` exit branches on `context.memory_call_id` to tell a tool round from the ambient one. What a caller sends with it is the recall shape `memory-hive` asks for (`hop.recall_query`, `hop.memory_tier`, `hop.recall_window_from`, `hop.recall_window_to`) plus the round it is asking in (`context.audience_set`, `context.channel`): a recall without an audience is not a recall with an empty one, and the hive refuses it rather than answering unfiltered. Whoever wires this lane owes it a drain -- `params.required_drains` pairs it with `bundle`, because for two waves this lane was a promise the level had no exit for and every answer to it died inside `./assistants`

the lane a generation of this member raises when it needs to read the memory -- declared here, since GH #562, so that nothing may carry it PAST this level. It is not a lane of this rim and never was: it starts inside `./assistants` and ends inside `./memory-hive`, both siblings in here, and `at` says so -- the one address it docks on at this level is the container. Under ADR-0020 a level that declares a lane takes part in it and may not be skipped, and taking part is exactly what this level does: the door `./assistants -> ./memory-hive` turns `recall` into the hive's own `in_query` and stamps the three keys the hive refuses a question without -- `audience_now` (the round, from `context.audience_set`), `channel` (the room) and `recall_as_of`. Nothing below this level knows the round and nothing above it knows the person, so a v-lane drawn from a generation's asker to any memory outside this member would produce `missing_audience` at runtime; it is refused at mutation time instead, with `v_lane_mandatory_hop`. The declaration is the sentence that does it

a read against this member's curated record: who is this person, who are they to the asker, what may this audience be told. It is answered from `affinity`, the holder of identity and meaning, and never from the memory -- memory produces, affinity decides. The asker and the ROUND are edge truth: the door promotes `context.asker` and `context.audience_set`, and a request that declares no round is refused with `no_round` rather than read as the asker alone

a write against that same record -- a correction, a trust or disclosure decision, a subscription. The writer is edge truth for the same reason the asker is: an audit row is only worth writing if its actor came from an edge rather than from body text, so the door promotes `context.actor` and, for a `subscribe`, `context.subscriber`

the builder's answer on its way back into the generation that asked. The member forwards it into `./assistants`; which generation it belongs to is decided by the per-instance edge inside that container, the same way `in_bundle` finds its way home. Derived from the accepts list of assistant@2.0.0

a demand that this member hand out everything it IS, as versioned documents. The lane crosses this level and lands on the `in_export` of THREE holders at once -- `./memory-hive` (what was said to this person), `./affinity` (the curated record that decides who may be told what) and `./firewall` (the screen every inbound turn passes) -- and, when the caller NAMES a generation in `context.assistant`, on a fourth: `./assistants`, through which the demand reaches that generation's own session keeper four levels down (GH #475). The generation is named rather than fanned to, for two reasons that are both measurable: a member with two assistants has two session ledgers and they are not one document, and the sink files a part under the hive it came out of, so two keepers would write one directory. An export that names none is the export this level always did, three holders and no dead letter -- the container is open and would have nowhere to deliver. Each walks its own tables and neither this level nor its neighbours decide what may leave: that is each hive's own walk (memory-hive@3.1.0 GH #243, affinity@3.2.0 and firewall@2.2.0 GH #471). Since GH #555 each holder's own STORE writes its seed set to disk, one directory per hive under the fence it declares, because a document that only exists as messages is not a backup -- this level owns no cell any more and files nothing. Until GH #471 only the memory hive answered this lane, and a member reborn from that export remembered everything it was told and knew nothing about who may be told it. The caller sends no keys with it -- every one of the three declares an empty context, and an export is about the whole member rather than about a round

one part of one of those documents, for a member that is already running. It is the other half of `in_export` and the return leg of the same document: the seed set under each holder was read once, when its `cell.db` was created, and is inert for ever after -- so everything the source learned or decided AFTER the walk (a delta, a correction, a second source) has no way in except a message. WHICH holder a part belongs to is edge truth: `hop.import_hive` names it ('affinity', 'firewall' or, since GH #475, 'session-keeper'), and a part that names none goes to the memory hive, which is the only place it could have come from before GH #471. A `session-keeper` part crosses into `./assistants`, and WHICH generation's keeper it lands in is decided by that container's own per-assistant edge on `context.assistant` -- the same key a turn is addressed with. A part that names the keeper and no generation has no address, and the container says so as `no_route` at its own path rather than being delivered to a holder that would refuse it under a misleading name. The member neither reads the part nor decides what may enter. The body is ONE export part, and applying the same part twice leaves the same state, which is what makes a partial transfer repairable by repeating it. The receipt rides the `dump` lane, and since GH #555 that lane LEAVES the level -- it used to end in a cell here that read it and said nothing about it. What a BIRTH needs instead of this lane is `examples/memory-import/`: a seed is a file, each holder is a `ref`, and a reference carries no files -- so a member born WITH a past is written out as a derived template, and a member already running cannot be given one

the `memory_recall` tool call a generation of this member made -- declared here, like `recall` above and for the same reason (GH #552, ADR-0020). It is not a lane of this rim and never was: it starts inside `./assistants` and ends inside `./memory-hive`, both siblings in here, and `at` says so. Under ADR-0020 a level that declares a lane takes part in it and may not be skipped, and taking part is exactly what this level does: the door `./assistants -> ./memory-hive` turns `tool` into the hive's own `tool_call` and stamps the two keys the hive refuses a question without -- `audience_now` (the round, from `context.audience_set`) and `channel` (the room). Nothing below this level knows the round and nothing above it knows the person, so a v-lane drawn from a generation straight to any memory would produce `missing_audience` at runtime; it is refused at mutation time instead, with `v_lane_mandatory_hop`

a generation's menu tick asking this member's memory what its tool looks like (GH #552). Same shape as `tool` and declared for the same reason: the question starts inside `./assistants`, the answer is written inside `./memory-hive`, and the door between them is this level's. A menu that never asked is a menu without `memory_recall` in it, and a round that then looks like a model which chose not to ask its memory

the mutation receipt, GH #553: the graph moved, and the door said so. This level declares it and routes it into `./assistants` AND `./apps` -- two children, because an agent's tool menu and a person's screen are the same fact read twice -- which is what makes it a mandatory hop under ADR-0020: nothing may carry this lane past a level that takes part in it. Derived from assistant@2.5.0 and colony-view@1.1.0

emits.because: what this member answered, from either of its two producers. From `./affinity` it is the brief the record produced, told apart from a push by `hop.subscriber == ''`; from `./assistants` it is a turn ANSWERED, and that half is new in 1.3.0 (GH #454). An answer whose turn arrived through one of this person's channels never gets here -- it is carried into `./channels` by the guarded edge and out through the channel that asked. What gets here is the other case: a turn injected at this member's own `in_turn` door, by an operator or a digest or a second person's agent, which names no channel of this member and whose answer therefore belongs to whoever sent it. That is a GUARDED DEFAULT (GH #283), not a second unconditional exit: exactly one of the two edges fires, and the one that fires is decided by whether `context.channel` names something. The lane was always declared at this level and at both levels above it -- org@1.4.0 and meclaw-os@1.6.1 both declare it -- and until 1.3.0 only the brief half could ever travel it, because the channel that consumed the answer stood inside the generation

the answer to a question this level's own `in_recall` door took: the recalled material, fused and ranked by `memory-hive`, on its way back to an asker OUTSIDE this member (GH #533). It leaves ONLY for that asker -- the exit is guarded on `hop.recall_caller == 'outside'`, the token the `in_recall` door stamped and the hive handed back on the hop (ADR-0019) -- and every other bundle takes the DEFAULT edge down into `./assistants`: an assistant's own, one carrying an unknown token, one carrying none at all. So the askers inside a generation are served exactly as they were before this lane existed, and this level never reads a token that belongs to the vocabulary of the level below it. Drain it: `params.required_drains` pairs it with `in_recall`, and a parent that wires the question without the answer has rebuilt the defect one level up. The exit RESTATES its own lane on the way out (`set_hop {"route": "'bundle'"}`, a no-op for the message): an exit guarded on a hop key the contract probe cannot carry is invisible to `hive_contract::exit_exists`, and GH #176's carve-out is exactly this -- an edge that NAMES the lane it carries is an exit whether or not a bare route probe can fire it. `./affinity -> .` on `answer` has been written that way since this level shipped

the way back of the lane above, declared here for the same reason and with the same effect (GH #562). The hive's `bundle` becomes `in_bundle` on the edge `./memory-hive -> ./assistants`, which is this level restamping a lane rather than forwarding it, and from the container one v-lane per asker carries it the last step. Like `recall` it is no lane of this rim -- both ends are inside -- so `at` names the container and nothing else: a v-lane that would deliver a bundle straight into a generation from OUTSIDE this member is a mandatory hop refused here, because the level that stamped the round on the way out is the level that owes the answer its way home
a proposed change to the record was accepted or rejected, with the reason code that says which. It leaves for the proposer

a refusal from one of this member's holders: a turn the screen refused (`hop.reject_reason`, `hop.rule_id`), or a question, block or turn the memory would not take (`hop.reject_reason` names the case). It is wired out of this level and consumed by NOBODY inside, and that is the honest state (2) of GH #284: a screened-off turn with no consumer is `no_route` in the DLQ, recorded and self-localising. `memory-hive` declares `required_drains` for `in_query`, `in_remember` and `in_episode`, so this lane also has to leave the level -- an undrained refusal is the one failure that gate exists to prevent Since 1.4.0 a third producer takes the lane: `./affinity` refuses a transfer it would not carry out (`hop.reject_reason` names the case), and `./firewall`'s own porter does the same on the lane the screen already uses. All three hives pair `in_export` and `in_import` with `reject` in their `required_drains`, so the edges out of them are not optional (GH #471). A session keeper's refusal does NOT arrive here: it is normalised inside the generation that holds it and crosses on `error` beside every other failure of that unit (GH #475). Since GH #533 the memory's refusal of a RECALL is sorted the same way its answer is: `hop.recall_caller == 'outside'` leaves here for the outside asker, and every other token -- an assistant's, an unknown one, none at all -- goes back DOWN into `./assistants` as `in_bundle` carrying `hop.reject_reason`, so the round that asked sees a typed refusal instead of waiting out its idle window for a bundle that will never come. Every other refusal this hive raises -- the writer's, the porter's, the close pass's -- carries no such token and leaves here as it always did

a failure that was not a refusal, from a holder of this member, from one of its CHANNELS or from one of its assistants; which cell inside produced it is not the caller's business. The member is a boundary, not a consumer -- an error that crosses it is one the parent owes a drain. Five sources, one lane, one declaration: `./affinity -> .`, `./channels -> .`, `./apps -> .`, `./access -> .` and `./assistants -> .`. The channel source arrived with GH #454: a connector's own failure used to leave through the generation that held it, and now that the connector is the person's it leaves beside the person's other failures. The assistant source is derived from the emits list of assistant@2.0.0

an assistant's batched conversation write, on its way past this member to whatever archive the parent wired. It is NOT this level's memory lane: the member's memory is written per turn on `extraction` and read on `in_recall`, both of which stop here. Derived from the emits list of assistant@2.0.0 -- nothing inside this member consumes it, so a level that did not declare it would let a real, recurring message die as no_route at its own boundary

one finished turn an assistant offers for archiving, one message per turn. Since GH #527 it is a FAN-OUT and no longer a pure pass-through, on the same terms as `write`: BOTH edges fire, because the same turn is this member's own episode below and the parent's archive above. The edge down is `./assistants -> ./memory-hive` on the hive's `in_episode`, and it is the only path in the substrate from a conversation into an `episodes` table (GH #298 removed every other one). RETRACTED with it, in the words this line carried until #527: `the member's own episode path is extraction -> the memory hive's in_remember, so this lane crosses the boundary untouched`. That was wrong in both halves. `in_remember` is the FACTS lane and it PRESUPPOSES episodes -- a block names no turn, so the ingress binds it to the newest `user` episode of the session and refuses every block while there is none -- and `write` -> `in_close_pass` is no second writer either, because nothing travels in its body and the pass reads the hive's OWN `episodes`. So the level that holds the memory (GH #122) declined the one lane that fills it, and a shipped colony dead-lettered every stored turn as `hive_no_route` at the OS root while its collector stamped each one `episode_written = 1`. `turn_id` comes off the HOP and not off the context: `context.turn_id` is a round uuid, `hop.turn_id` is the deterministic `<session_id>#<index>` the collector mints, and it is what the inline bind and the queue row are keyed on -- an edge that promoted the context key would write episodes nothing can ever bind to, a defect that looks exactly like this one from the outside. The lane still LEAVES the level unchanged, so a parent that wants an archive of its own still gets one. Derived from the emits list of assistant@2.0.0

an assistant's housekeeping report, raised when something upstream fired its `in_prune` lane. This member owns no timer and fires nothing, so it neither produces this lane nor consumes it -- it only refuses to swallow it. Derived from the emits list of assistant@2.0.0

a structural wish or a submission leaving one of this person's generations. The member neither reads it nor answers it: the builder is at the OS level because one colony has one baumeister, and everything between is transit. Derived from the emits list of assistant@2.0.0

the receipt of one close pass: how many facts the strong model added, sharpened, corrected, closed or restated when it read an ended session whole. It is raised by this member's memory hive and consumed by NOBODY inside -- the member triggers the pass but is not its reader, and `memory-hive` declares `required_drains` for `in_close_pass` -> `close_report`, so an undrained receipt would refuse the very mutation that wires the close pass. Undrained ABOVE this level it becomes no_route in the DLQ, which is state (2) of GH #284: recorded and self-localising

one of this member's holders has written itself out completely: every table of its walk stands as `<seed_dir>/<table>.jsonl` under the fence that holder's own store declares, and the completion marker `export_final.json` stands beside them, written last (GH #555). `hop.export_hive` names which holder finished, `hop.seed_dir` says where, relative to that fence. It is the one lane that says an export is a BACKUP rather than a stack of messages, and it leaves the level because whoever demanded the export is outside it. THREE travel per export, one per holder -- FOUR when the caller named a generation in `context.assistant` and that generation's session keeper wrote its ledger out beside them (GH #475) -- and they arrive in whatever order the walks finish in -- the holder that finished says so ITSELF since 1.6.0, where before a sink cell of this level said it for all of them

the receipt of one applied import part, from whichever holder took it -- `hop.rows_written` counts the inserts it dispatched, so zero means the target already had every row. It is the only positive signal an import has, and it LEAVES the level because whoever sent the document is outside it. Until 1.6.0 it ended inside this member, in a `code` cell that read it and said nothing about it -- the one arrangement GH #284 forbids -- and it ended there only because that cell existed for the EXPORT half. The export writes its own files now (GH #555), so the receipt travels the way every other receipt of this level does. FOUR senders: the three holders and, for a named generation, `./assistants`

the receipt of one identity pack, from a generation this member's own `./affinity` pushed to (GH #458). The member does NOT consume it, and that is the decision rather than an omission: affinity's own record of a delivery is the `sent_at` stamp it writes itself, and the hive has no lane that takes a receipt -- so a receipt is evidence for whoever operates the colony, and it leaves the level the way `prune` and `error` do. TWO travel per pack, one per occupant of the generation, because `in_pack` fans out to the surface and the core inside the assistant. Derived from the emits list of assistant@2.2.0 -- nothing inside this member consumes it, so a level that did not declare it would let a real, recurring message die as no_route at its own boundary

the way back of `tool`, declared here for the same reason and with the same effect (GH #552). The hive's `tool_result` becomes `in_tool` on the edge `./memory-hive -> ./assistants`, which is this level restamping a lane rather than forwarding it: the result re-enters the asking round as an ordinary tool result, refusals included, and the round ends where it began

the way back of `schemas` (GH #552). The hive's `tool_schemas` becomes `in_menu` on the edge `./memory-hive -> ./assistants` and carries `context.tool_answerer == 'memory'`, which is the key the menu merge of GH #529 files an answerer's declarations under -- without it a third answerer would overwrite the menu instead of joining it

required_drains.because: a question sent at this member's own recall door is answered OUT of the level, and until GH #533 there was nowhere for that answer to go: `bundle` was not an emits lane, so the one return edge the level had carried it into `./assistants`, where it died as `no_route` -- or, worse, was handed to whichever generation `context.assistant` happened to name. A caller that asks and does not subscribe to the answer rebuilds that failure one level up. The trigger is the caller's STAMP (GH #237): a parent that names this lane in a condition instead is not caught here, which is why the shipped recipes are pinned by `gh533_the_outside_asker_gets_an_answer.rs` as well

description.purpose: One person, and the things every assistant that person owns must share: the memory of what was said to them, the curated record of who they and their people are, the screen every inbound turn passes, and -- since 1.3.0 -- the CHANNELS they are reached on. Three refs plus three open containers -- `assistants`, `channels` and, since GH #459, `apps` -- plus one cell of its own: the sink that turns a memory export into files on disk. The level owns nothing else -- no brain, no tools. Since GH #475 the transfer lanes reach one thing more: a generation's session keeper, four levels down, through `./assistants` -- the sessions are the last table of a member that a rebuild could not recompute. Since member@1.5.0 the level also carries an `access` of its own (GH #560). Authorisation and key ownership are two different jobs: the shell's broker answers the submitter's policy questions, but the provider keys this person's brains burn belong to the PERSON -- the same ADR-0013 logic that puts the memory hive at this level. Nothing in this graph reaches it except the drain for its `error` lane, and that is deliberate: the two edges that carry a credential are V-LANES (GH #559), drawn by the manifest that grows a generation, from the brain that spends the grant straight to `./access`. See README section `The credential v-lanes`.
description.use_when: One per person (or per group that owns an agent nobody owns personally -- that group is a member with its own name). Instantiate it into an org's members container, and wire its eight inbound lanes and its thirteen outbound ones in the same mutation -- the three refusal and receipt lanes above all (`reject`, `close_report`, `export_done`), because `memory-hive` pairs every ingress this level sends with an egress the level above has to take, and an undrained pairing refuses the mutation rather than the message. `bundle` is the twelfth and youngest of them (GH #533) and this level pairs it itself: it is the answer to a question sent at the `in_recall` door, and a caller that asks and does not subscribe gets the answer nowhere. Assistants are instantiated into ./assistants afterwards, one at a time, and each of those mutations draws its own two addressing edges to the container. Channels are instantiated into ./channels the same way, one at a time, and each of those draws two edges as well -- see templates/member/README.md, 'Addressing an assistant through a channel'.
description.not_in_scope: No brain and no tool surface -- those are the assistant's, and one member may own several. No memory-drain: per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced it, and it does not belong in the assistant either. No terminal: a refusal here leaves the level and becomes no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes it -- recorded and self-localising, which is state (2) of GH #284. And since 1.6.0 there is no cell here at all to be a counter-example: the one that landed an export on disk is gone, because every store writes its own files (GH #555). No org-level anything: what a group knows about a person is a filter on the read, never a second store. The push into a subscribing brain is this level's to own and the instantiating mutation's to draw (GH #453): a subscribe writes a row, never an edge, so the two edges of the recipe are drawn per subscribing cell at instantiation (templates/affinity/README.md, 'Wiring out_push for a subscribing brain'). This level ships the half a template CAN ship -- the answer exit conditioned on hop.subscriber == '', so a push can never leave on the brief lane.
